(PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI) Appellant who is arraigned as accused No.1 has filed this appeal under Section this petition filed under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure (for short, 'the Cr.P.C.') (483 of BNSS), seeking regular bail in Crime No.88/2024 for the offences punishable under Section 420 of IPC and Section 3(2)(va) of SC/ST Act 2015.
2. In support of the appeal, the appellant has contended that there is no prima facie case made out against the appellant.
He was in live in relationship with the complainant and the same is converted as a case of cheating.
The complaint averments, statement of complainant under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and her further statement contradict each other.
Appellant has no criminal antecedents.
The alleged offences are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
No justifiable reasons are NC: 2024:KHC-D:18110 given by the Trial Court for rejecting his bail application.
Already charge sheet is filed and as such, the custodial presence of the appellant is not required.
He is permanent resident of the address given in the cause title.
3. He is ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and offer substantial surety to the satisfaction of the trial Court and pray to allow the appeal.
4. Learned HCGP submitted oral objections stating that complainant belongs to Hindu Arunashikari coming under scheduled tribe.
She is married and having two children.
However, she fell in love with the appellant and during September 2018, they started living together at Naragund.
On 05.09.2018, at 6.00 pm, the parents and elder sister of accused No.1 picked up quarrel with her.
They abused her referring to her caste and also assaulted her.
Since she was having good relationship with accused No.1, she did not file any complaint.

On 07.02.2022, both of them went to Sri Mailarlingeshwara temple, Mailar of NC: 2024:KHC-D:18110 Huvinahadagali and accused no.1 Sangameshwar S/O Ningappa Hallur vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143363389/
2 married her by tying Tali.

sentences.text: Thereafter, they shifted to Kerala and staying in a room belonging to Mammacha at Charakala.
They live together for six years.
They had physical relationship.
5. It is the further case of the prosecution that since one year, appellant started harassing and ill-treating the complainant.
He used to assault her listening to his sister.
He snatched away Rs.47,000/- from her.
On 04.05.2024 at 8.00 pm, appellant abused and assaulted her.
He snatched away Rs.15,000/- and left to Tirlapura on 05.05.2024.
He even switched off his phone and therefore, she is filing the complaint at Navalgund.
6. Based on the complaint, the concerned police have conducted detailed investigation and filed charge sheet against the appellant.
His parents and sister are given up.
There is prima facie material to proceed against the appellant for the offences punishable under Sections Section 420 of IPC and Section 3(2)(va) of SC/ST Act 2015.

In the event of granting bail, the appellant may NC:
2024:KHC-D:18110 threaten or temper with the witnesses.
He may also abscond and thereby delay and defeat the investigation and trial and pray to reject the appeal.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the record.
8.

From the complaint averments and charge sheet, it is the definite case of the prosecution that though complainant is a married woman having husband and children, she fell in love with the appellant and started living with him.
For six months they stayed together at Naragund.
It is alleged that when the parents and elder sister of appellant objected them for living together, they shifted to Kerala and lived together for six years.

Now, alleging that the appellant has snatched Rs.47,000/-
and Rs.15,000/- from the complainant and left to Tirlapur.
He even stopped communicating with her by switching of his cell phone and therefore, she has filed the complaint.
9. After conducting detailed investigation, the concerned police have filed charge sheet against the NC: 2024:KHC-D:18110 appellant.
The parents and elder sister of the appellant are non charge sheeted and only appellant is sent up for trial.

Having regard to the nature of the allegations made,
the investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed, no longer the custodial presence of the appellant is required.

Having regard to the specific case of the prosecution that the complainant is already married and in her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she has stated that appellant has tied Tali to her at Sri Mailarlingeshwara temple, whether the offence under Section 420 of IPC that the appellant has cheated her by developing physical relationship under promise of marriage is attracted is a matter to be decided at the time of framing charge.
For the above reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that this is a fit case to grant bail to the appellant.
10. Of course, there is apprehension on the part of the prosecution that the appellant may threaten or temper with the witnesses.
He may also abscond and thereby delay the proceedings.

These may be overcome by NC: 2024:KHC-D:18110 imposing stringent conditions, and accordingly, the following;
ORDER Appeal is allowed.
